title: Validated environment-based configuration with fail-fast startup

blocks.text: External configuration needs validation. Subclass pydantic_settings.BaseSettings and declare typed fields. Construct Settings() to read environment variables and validate them; missing required settings or invalid values fail validation.
For dotenv input, set model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env"). Environment variables take precedence over dotenv values.

blocks.code:
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict

class Settings(BaseSettings):
    app_name: str
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env")

settings = Settings()

blocks.text: Check construction with a valid environment setting, a missing required setting and a value incompatible with its declared type. Missing or invalid configuration fails validation instead of becoming unchecked input.

With dotenv enabled, compare conflicting values for the same key. The environment wins, but source priority does not remove type validation. Identify both the supplying source and whether its value satisfies the declaration.
Declare the required typed app_name field on Settings, configure the dotenv file, and construct Settings(). This reads and validates external input.

The registered source cases separate environment-only, conflicting-source and absent-from-both conditions. An environment value wins a conflict with dotenv. If a required value is absent, construction fails; an incompatible value also fails validation. A dotenv file is not an override for the environment.

segments.label: Declare typed settings and replace a default through the environment
segments.summary: A configuration module defines Settings by importing BaseSettings from pydantic_settings and subclassing it. The class declares app_name as a string with a default. Constructing Settings creates an object whose fields can be accessed by the application. The example first uses the default name, then supplies APP_NAME in the environment for a command. The resulting settings object uses that environment value instead of the default.

bridge.before: Watch how the typed app_name declaration becomes a constructed settings object. The clip uses a default; the text also teaches required settings without defaults.
bridge.after: The clip demonstrates environment loading, but not missing-required or invalid-value failures, dotenv configuration, or dotenv precedence. The text covers those rules so configuration can be validated before serving.
